summary:
Aurora is a browser-based educational space mission design and operations game that transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an interactive learning experience.
Players choose from five scientific mission scenarios, design spacecraft, select scientific instruments, balance mass, power, data, communications, and budget, choose launch vehicles and orbits, operate missions, and analyze their final results.
Aurora integrates NASA mission-segment concepts and an educational adaptation of JPL's Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4). It also features numerical Earth–Moon orbital simulations using the Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP), helping players explore the engineering decisions behind real space missions.
Aurora makes space mission engineering more accessible through interactive gameplay, scientific visualization, and experimentation.
details: Project Overview Aurora is an interactive browser-based educational game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, under the Space Mission Design Game challenge. The project addresses the difficulty of understanding how scientific objectives, spacecraft engineering, launch systems, orbital selection, communications, and limited resources interact throughout a complete space mission. Gameplay and Mission Design Aurora organizes the mission lifecycle into four interconnected segments: - User Segment: Select scientific objectives and mission requirements. - Space Segment: Design the spacecraft and select its components and scientific instruments. - Launch Segment: Choose a suitable launch vehicle and orbital destination. - Ground Segment: Select ground communication networks and operate the mission. Players manage critical mission resources, including mass, power, battery capacity, budget, data generation, communications, and delta-v. The game includes five mission scenarios: 1. CubeSat Classroom 2. Wildfire Watch 3. Lunar Relay 4. Asteroid Scout 5. Red Planet Weather It supports solo, local co-op, online co-op, versus challenge, and sandbox gameplay modes. Scientific and Engineering Foundation Aurora incorporates an educational Earth–Moon Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP) model. The orbital simulation includes: - JPL DE440 Earth and Moon gravitational parameters. - Adaptive Dormand–Prince 5(4) numerical integration. - Numerical Lagrange L2 equilibrium calculations. - Jacobi constant monitoring. - Numerically propagated NRHO and L2 halo reference trajectories. - Comparisons with published NASA Gateway NRHO orbital characteristics. Aurora also adapts JPL's Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4) into an educational progression system that helps players understand how mission concepts develop from initial ideas toward more detailed designs. Technology The application is built using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, with Three.js for interactive 3D visualization. It includes Progressive Web App functionality and an offline-cached game interface. Cloudflare Workers, D1, and Durable Objects provide the backend architecture for online functionality. Testing and Validation The project validation report records 42 automated tests passed, covering mission simulation, orbital mechanics, application assets, and database-related logic. Local code and database checks were completed. Remote cloud deployment, real-device Android testing, and live multiplayer infrastructure testing remain deployment-dependent. Educational Impact Aurora aims to make aerospace engineering more accessible by allowing learners to experiment with spacecraft configurations, understand engineering trade-offs, explore orbital dynamics, and evaluate the consequences of mission decisions. It encourages STEM education, systems thinking, scientific curiosity, and collaborative problem-solving. Project Availability The source code is publicly available on GitHub under the MIT License: https://github.com/mustafasameh369-sketch/Aurora Aurora is an independent educational project and is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by NASA. Aurora — Design the mission. Balance every trade-off. Own every decision.
